title: Validate kernel_size matches weight dims in slow_conv_transpose3d
body:
Fixes #142457

## Summary

`slow_conv_transpose3d` accepts `kernel_size` as an explicit argument separate from the weight tensor. When these disagree (e.g. `kernel_size=[1,1,1]` but weight has spatial dims `[2,3,2]`), the columns buffer is allocated using `kernel_size` while the GEMM uses `weight.sizes()`, causing a buffer size mismatch that leads to memory corruption ("double free or corruption" / abort).

This adds a `TORCH_CHECK` in both the CPU and CUDA `slow_conv_transpose3d_shape_check` functions to validate that `kernel_size` matches `weight.size(2:4)`, raising a clear error instead of crashing. This mirrors the existing check in `DepthwiseConv3d`.

## Changes

- `aten/src/ATen/native/NaiveConvolutionTranspose3d.cpp` — add kernel_size vs weight spatial dims check
- `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/NaiveConvolutionTranspose3d.cu` — same check for CUDA path
- `test/nn/test_convolution.py` — add test calling `aten.slow_conv_transpose3d` with mismatched kernel_size

## Test plan

The new test `test_slow_conv_transpose3d_kernel_size_mismatch` calls `torch.ops.aten.slow_conv_transpose3d` with the exact inputs from the issue (kernel_size `[1,1,1]` vs weight spatial `[2,3,2]`) and asserts a `RuntimeError` is raised instead of crashing.

cc @mikaylagawarecki
